options.title: Salvator Mundi sold for {fact3}. Then for {fact1} 🖼️
options.first_line: This painting, Salvator Mundi, once sold for just {fact3}.
options.first_frame: A junk shop's back room: the painting of a robed figure holding a glass orb leans against a crate with a paper price tag of the pound figure, its title plate reading 'SALVATOR MUNDI'.

options.title: The {fact1} painting that once sold for {fact3}
options.first_line: Salvator Mundi sold for {fact1}, and it once went for {fact3}.
options.first_frame: An auction room's price board blazing the record figure above the painting of a robed figure holding a glass orb, a tiny old price tag of the pound figure still stuck to its frame.

options.title: Sold as a copy for {fact3}. Sold as a Leonardo for {fact1}
options.first_line: Salvator Mundi was sold as a copy for {fact3}, then as a Leonardo da Vinci for {fact1}.
options.first_frame: The painting split down the middle: the left half brown and painted over with a 'COPY' stamp and the pound tag, the right half clean and glowing under a 'LEONARDO DA VINCI' plate.

why: It names Leonardo da Vinci, whom every stranger knows, and the jump from a copy at the small price to a Leonardo at the record poses the mystery of how the same painting changed identity, which the split first frame shows even with the sound off.
